study type: Cohort study (secondary analysis of merged randomized prospective trial data)
exposure: Estimated quantity of oxytocin administered during labor
outcome: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) of 500 mL or more
Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) of 1000 mL or more
cohort: The study included 9209 women who had a vaginal delivery, drawn from the merged database of three randomized prospective trials (TRACOR, CYTOCINON, and TRAAP) where postpartum blood loss was precisely measured.
finding: Among women with vaginal delivery, induction of labor was associated with a significantly higher risk of postpartum hemorrhage (both >=500 mL and >=1000 mL), regardless of the method of induction.
mod_finding: 34% of the association between IOL and PPH was mediated by the quantity of oxytocin administered during labor, and 1.3% was mediated by operative vaginal delivery.
